title: Water and energy efficiency
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Any worker or owner in any service business who uses water and energy in the course of service work.
learningOutcomes: Use water and energy efficiently during a job without reducing the quality or safety of the work.
Describe the common sources of water and energy waste on service jobs.
Check the water-use restrictions and discharge rules that apply before using water on site.

instruction.heading: Water use on a job
instruction.body: Water is used to mix products, rinse surfaces, fill buckets and run equipment. Waste usually comes from running taps, rinsing longer than needed, filling buckets to the top, and using a hose where a bucket and cloth would do. Use a bucket method for most cleaning, and change the water when it becomes soiled. Use a trigger spray with the minimum volume that wets the surface. Check whether the site has water-use restrictions, and do not use water where a restriction applies or where the discharge route is not approved.

instruction.heading: Energy use on a job
instruction.body: Energy is used by vacuums, pressure washers, floor machines, heaters, dryers and lighting. Switch off equipment when it is not in use, and do not leave a machine running while you move between rooms. Use the lowest effective setting for each machine, and keep filters and brushes clean so that the machine works efficiently. Turn off lights in areas you have finished where the customer agrees and the work is not affected. Check equipment for faults that increase energy use, such as a motor that runs hot, and record the fault.

instruction.heading: Efficiency and safety
instruction.body: Efficiency must not reduce safety or quality. Do not reduce water or the rinse step where the product label or the procedure requires it. Do not turn off ventilation or lighting where it is needed for safe work. Where a machine has a setting that reduces energy but reduces its effectiveness, test it on a hidden area and record the result before using it on the visible area.

procedure: Check the site for water-use restrictions and the approved discharge route before using water.
Use a bucket method and trigger sprays, using the minimum water that does the job.
Change soiled water and do not reuse it for a different zone.
Switch off equipment when not in use, and set machines to the lowest effective setting.
Keep filters and brushes clean so that machines run efficiently.
Record any equipment fault that increases water or energy use, and report it.

workedExamples.situation: A customer asks you to hose down the outdoor patio, which is currently under a water-use restriction.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not use the hose while the restriction applies. Use a method the restriction allows, such as a bucket and a brush, and tell the customer. Record the restriction and the method used.

equipmentAndPpe: Cloths and brushes suited to the surface

commonErrors.error: Running a hose or tap continuously while cleaning.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a bucket and stop the flow when not needed.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a machine running while moving between rooms.
commonErrors.prevention: Switch off the machine when you leave it.

commonErrors.error: Cutting the rinse step to save water where the label requires it.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the label and procedure rinse requirements, and save water elsewhere.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Water-use restrictions and trade waste discharge rules are set by water authorities, councils and state or territory law, and must be checked for each location.
Efficiency measures for electrical equipment must not involve modifying the equipment or its safety devices. Report any fault and do not bypass a safety device to save energy.

qualityStandard: Water and energy use is kept to the level the job needs.
No rinse or ventilation step is reduced below the label or procedure requirement.
Equipment faults that increase use are recorded and reported.
documentationEvidence: Record of any water-use restriction on site and the method used.
Equipment fault record for any item that uses unusual energy or water.
summary: Use a bucket and trigger sprays, and stop the flow when not needed.
Switch off equipment when not in use and keep it clean and efficient.
Never reduce a required rinse, ventilation or safety step to save resources.

knowledgeChecks.question: The site has a water-use restriction. What should you do?
options: Use the hose anyway for a short time.
Use a method the restriction allows and tell the customer.
Use the normal method, since small jobs are exempt from restrictions

knowledgeChecks.question: Which action is correct when moving between rooms?
options: Turn the machine to its highest setting.
Switch off the machine when you leave it.
